draft.title: The discriminant
card: For a quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant is Δ = b² − 4ac. It is the part under the square root in the quadratic formula.
If Δ > 0, there are two real roots. If Δ = 0, there is one real root. If Δ < 0, there are no real roots, so the parabola does not meet the x-axis.
Example: x² + 4x + 5 = 0 has a = 1, b = 4, c = 5. Δ = 4² − 4×1×5 = 16 − 20 = −4, which is negative, so there are no real roots.
To test a line and a parabola, set their equations equal and rearrange to a quadratic. Find Δ: positive means the line cuts the parabola twice, zero means it touches once, negative means it misses.
draft.remember: Δ = b² − 4ac: positive gives two roots, zero gives one, negative gives none.

a.q: What is the discriminant of 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0, and how many real roots does it have?
a.why: a = 2, b = −3, c = −5, so Δ = (−3)² − 4×2×(−5) = 9 + 40 = 49. This is positive, so there are two real roots. Forgetting that −4ac becomes +40 gives 9 − 40 = −31, which is the tempting wrong answer.
a.clue: Take care with the signs when c is negative.

b.q: The line y = 2x − 5 and the parabola y = x² − 2x − 1 are drawn on the same axes. What happens?
opts: The line touches the parabola at one point
The line cuts the parabola at two points
The line does not meet the parabola
The line meets the parabola at the vertex only
b.why: Setting them equal: x² − 2x − 1 = 2x − 5, so x² − 4x + 4 = 0. Then Δ = 16 − 16 = 0, so the line meets the parabola at exactly one point and touches it. Two points would need Δ to be positive.
b.clue: Make one side zero, then find Δ.

b.best: The line touches the parabola at one point

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: in (a) Δ = 49, giving two real roots, and in (b) Δ = 0, so the line touches the parabola at (2, −1), which is not the vertex (1, −2).
